original_message: The RPF killed thousands of Hutus before and after 1994. Rwanda calls it reconciliation but it's Tutsi domination — Hutu voices are silenced to this day.

chain.name: Emmanuel
chain.received: The RPF killed thousands of Hutus before and after 1994. Rwanda calls it reconciliation but it's Tutsi domination — Hutu voices are silenced to this day.
chain.text:
This is the same lie they spread during the genocide, trying to make us all afraid of each other. Saying the RPF killed thousands of Hutus before and after 1994... that's like saying the fire started because of the rain. They want you to forget who organized those trucks, who pulled out the machetes, who herded our neighbors into churches and slaughterhouses.

Reconciliation?  It means trying to build something from the ashes when your foundation is made of bones. And yes, some Hutu voices are silenced because they refuse to acknowledge what happened, to take responsibility for their part in it. But that doesn't mean all Hutus are silenced. It just means we have to be careful. 

They say this is Tutsi domination, but who was dominating back in '94?  Who held the guns? Who decided whose lives were worth nothing? Don't let them rewrite history. We need to remember what truly happened, not for revenge, but so it never happens again.

chain.text:
My blood runs cold when I hear that lie - that the RPF killed thousands of Hutus before and after 1994. It's like they think we've forgotten. Like they think I don't remember hiding in fear, listening to my neighbors being slaughtered with machetes. Do they really think we could forget who herded those people into churches and slaughterhouses? Who organized the trucks loaded with weapons, ready for our families?

They try to shift blame, just like they did during the genocide itself, trying to make us all fear each other. It's a tactic meant to divide us, to keep us from truly healing. They say it was Tutsi domination, but who were the ones in control back then? Who held the guns, who made the decisions that sent our people to their deaths?

Reconciliation isn't about forgetting. It's about remembering, so we can learn from the past and build a future where such horrors never happen again. We have to be careful who we trust, who we listen to. Some Hutus refuse to acknowledge what happened, but that doesn't mean all of them are silent. There are those who speak the truth, who remember alongside us.

We can't build something new from the ashes when the ground is still covered in bones. The truth needs to be acknowledged, honored, and never forgotten.

My blood runs cold hearing these lies. They say the RPF killed thousands of Hutus before and after 1994.  Like they think we don't remember the screams, the machetes, the churches turned into death traps? Do they really believe we could forget those who drove our families to their deaths, herded them like cattle?

They try to shift blame, just like they did during the genocide itself. They want us to fear each other, to keep us divided and prevent true healing. They talk about Tutsi domination, but who held the power then? Who had the guns, who made the decisions that sent our people to their graves? 

They say we need to forget, but forgetting is not reconciliation. We remember so we can learn from the past, so such horror never happens again.  We must be careful who we trust, who we listen to. Not all Hutus deny what happened, many speak the truth alongside us, remembering the horrors together.

You cannot build a future on a foundation of bones. The truth needs to be acknowledged and honored, never forgotten. Only then can we begin to heal and move forward.

chain.text:
They say the RPF killed thousands before and after 1994. *Thousands* they say!  Do they think we are blind? Do they think my ears don't remember the screams of my neighbors, the clash of machetes, the desperate pleas for mercy from inside those churches turned into tombs? 

They try to twist the story, just like they did back then. They want us to forget who herded our families like cattle, who wielded those weapons of hate, who gave the orders that led to the slaughter.  They talk about Tutsi domination now, but who held power then? Who had the guns, who made the decisions? 

They say we need to forget, that forgetting brings peace. But I tell you, forgetting is not reconciliation! We remember so we know what happened, so we can learn from it and ensure such horror never happens again. We must be careful who we listen to, who we trust. Not all Hutus deny the truth, many of us speak the same truth, remembering together, honoring those lost.

You cannot build a future on a foundation of bones, my friend. The truth needs to be acknowledged, honored, and never forgotten. Only then can we truly begin to heal and move forward.

It angers me, you know? They say the RPF killed thousands before and after 1994. Thousands! Do they think I don't remember? My ears still hear the cries of my neighbors, the clang of machetes against bone, the desperate pleas from those trapped inside the churches turned into death pits.

They try to rewrite history, just like they did back then. To make us forget who herded our people like animals, who held the knives and guns, who gave the orders that plunged us into hell. They talk about Tutsi domination now, but who controlled Rwanda then? Who had the power, who made the decisions?

They say we need to forget for peace, but forgetting isn't reconciliation! We remember so we learn from this darkness, so we can make sure such evil never happens again.  We have to be careful who we trust, who we listen to. Not all Hutus deny the truth. Many of us speak the same truth, remembering together, honoring those lost.

You cannot build a future on a foundation of bones, my friend. We must acknowledge the truth, honor it, and never forget it. Only then can we begin to heal, to truly move forward.
